claim: In a consecutive single-centre series of 58 patients with mesial TLE treated with stereotactic laser amygdalohippocampotomy (>=12 months follow-up), 53.4% were Engel I at 1 year (60.5% with vs 33.3% without mesial temporal sclerosis).

bibliographic_record.authors: Gross RE, Stern MA, Willie JT, Fasano RE, Saindane AM, Soares BP, Pedersen NP, Drane DL
bibliographic_record.title: Stereotactic laser amygdalohippocampotomy for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy

supporting_passage: One year following stereotactic laser amygdalohippocampotomy, 53.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 40.8-65.7%) of all patients were free of disabling seizures (Engel I).
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 29420840; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/29420840; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: retrospective review of a consecutive single-centre series (Emory), 5-year period
population_and_design.population: mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, >=12 months follow-up

reported_observation: 53.4% Engel I at 1 year; MTS 60.5% vs non-MTS 33.3%.
author_inference: Seizure-free rates lower than, but comparable to, open temporal lobe surgery; verbal memory outcome better than historical open-resection data (historical comparison, not randomised).
contradictions: MTS associated with better outcome here, whereas Wu 2019 multicenter found radiographic hippocampal sclerosis not associated with outcome.
